result.target_topic: Valuation allowance and effective tax rate change
result.target_summary: The effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to the establishment of a valuation allowance against US federal deferred tax assets in 2024. This allowance was recognized in the third quarter of 2024 after determining it was more likely than not that the assets would not be recoverable, largely due to a three-year cumulative historical loss position resulting from asset impairment and restructuring charges.

comparisons.peer_topic: Deferred tax asset valuation allowance policy
comparisons.peer_summary: A valuation allowance is recorded for deferred tax assets unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not; conversely, if realization is deemed more-likely-than-not, existing valuation allowances may be reversed, resulting in a credit to income tax expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose their policy for assessing the recoverability of deferred tax assets and recording valuation allowances based on a 'more-likely-than-not' threshold. Intel describes a specific 2024 event where this assessment led to establishing an allowance against US federal deferred tax assets due to historical losses from impairments. AMD discloses the general policy that such allowances are recorded unless recovery is more-likely-than-not, and that reversal of these allowances results in a credit to income tax expense. While Intel provides specific factual outcomes of its assessment in 2024, AMD outlines the operational mechanics and reversal consequences of the policy.

sentences.text: Our effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by the effects associated with the establishment of a valuation allowance against our US federal deferred tax assets in 2024.

As a result of our assessment in the third quarter of 2024, we determined it was more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable based upon our three-year cumulative historical loss position as of the third quarter of 2024, largely resulting from the asset impairment and restructuring and other charges incurred during the third quarter of 2024.

Unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not (a probability level of more than 50%), we will record a charge to income tax expense in the form of a valuation allowance for the deferred tax assets that we estimate will not ultimately be recoverable or maintain the valuation allowance recorded in prior periods.

When considering all available evidence, if we determine it is more-likely-than-not we will realize our deferred tax assets, we will reverse some or all of the existing valuation allowance, which would result in a credit to income tax expense and the establishment of an asset in the period of reversal.

comparisons.peer_summary: Significant management judgment is required to determine income tax provisions, deferred tax assets/liabilities, and valuation allowances, considering future taxable income and tax planning strategies.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom (AVGO) identify valuation allowances against deferred tax assets as a significant area requiring management judgment and assessment. Intel's disclosure details the specific determination in Q3 2024 that deferred tax assets were not recoverable based on a three-year cumulative loss position, leading to a valuation allowance. Broadcom similarly states that significant management judgment is required in determining valuation allowances, considering projected future taxable income and tax planning strategies. Both companies address the same specific topic of assessing and recognizing valuation allowances for deferred tax assets.

sentences.text: Our effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by the effects associated with the establishment of a valuation allowance against our US federal deferred tax assets in 2024.

As a result of our assessment in the third quarter of 2024, we determined it was more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable based upon our three-year cumulative historical loss position as of the third quarter of 2024, largely resulting from the asset impairment and restructuring and other charges incurred during the third quarter of 2024.

Significant management judgment is required in developing our provision for or benefit from income taxes, including the determination of deferred tax assets and liabilities and any valuation allowances that might be required against the deferred tax assets.
We have considered projected future taxable income and ongoing prudent and feasible tax planning strategies in assessing the need for valuation allowances.

comparisons.peer_topic: Income taxes and deferred tax asset realizability
comparisons.peer_summary: Estimating income tax provisions and deferred tax assets requires significant judgment and depends on the ability to generate future taxable income in jurisdictions like Japan, the US, Malaysia, and Taiwan.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron (MU) discuss the judgment involved in evaluating the realizability of deferred tax assets. Intel specifically notes that its assessment in Q3 2024 determined it was 'more likely than not' that US federal deferred tax assets would not be recoverable due to historical losses. Micron states that evaluating realizability 'requires the assessment of our performance' and that realization depends on generating future taxable income, which involves significant judgments regarding forecasts. Both disclosures center on the same specific topic: the criteria and judgment required to determine if deferred tax assets can be realized (i.e., whether to maintain or record a valuation allowance).

sentences.text: We assess the recoverability of our deferred tax assets quarterly, weighing available positive and negative evidence.

As a result of our assessment in the third quarter of 2024, we determined it was more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable based upon our three-year cumulative historical loss position as of the third quarter of 2024, largely resulting from the asset impairment and restructuring and other charges incurred during the third quarter of 2024.

We are also required to evaluate the realizability of our deferred tax assets on an ongoing basis in accordance with U.S. GAAP, which requires the assessment of our performance and other relevant factors.
Realization of deferred tax assets is dependent on our ability to generate future taxable income.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation allowance for deferred tax assets
comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, the company maintained valuation allowances of $1.6 billion and $1.5 billion, respectively, related to capital loss carryforwards and certain state and other deferred tax assets determined not likely to be realized. If realization becomes more-likely-than-not, such deferred tax assets would be recognized as income tax benefits during the period.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA (NVDA) disclose the maintenance of valuation allowances for deferred tax assets that management determined are not likely to be realized. Intel's 2024 disclosure explicitly states the establishment of a valuation allowance against US federal deferred tax assets because they were not likely to be recoverable. NVIDIA discloses that it maintained valuation allowances of $1.6 billion (2024) and $1.5 billion (2023) related to capital loss carryforwards and other deferred tax assets because management determined they were 'not likely to be realized.' Both companies address the specific topic of recognizing valuation allowances for specific deferred tax assets based on realizability assessments.

sentences.text: Our effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by the effects associated with the establishment of a valuation allowance against our US federal deferred tax assets in 2024.

As a result of our assessment in the third quarter of 2024, we determined it was more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable based upon our three-year cumulative historical loss position as of the third quarter of 2024, largely resulting from the asset impairment and restructuring and other charges incurred during the third quarter of 2024.

As of the end of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, we had a valuation allowance of $1.6 billion and $1.5 billion, respectively, related to capital loss carryforwards, and certain state and other deferred tax assets that management determined are not likely to be realized due, in part, to jurisdictional projections of future taxable income, including capital gains.
To the extent realization of the deferred tax assets becomes more-likely-than-not, we would recognize such deferred tax assets as income tax benefits during the period.
